mockData.content: Artificial Intelligence is transforming the modern world by enabling machines to simulate human intelligence and perform complex tasks efficiently. mockData.title: Machine Learning vs Deep Learning
mockData.subtitle: Understanding the key differences between two major branches of Artificial Intelligence.

left.title: Machine Learning
left.description: Machine learning uses algorithms to analyze data and make predictions with minimal human intervention.
points: Requires structured and labeled data.
Works well with smaller datasets.
Training time is generally faster.
Feature extraction is often manual.

right.title: Deep Learning
right.description: Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to automatically learn complex patterns from data.
points: Handles large and unstructured datasets effectively.
Requires higher computational power.
Automatically extracts features from data.
Commonly used in image and speech recognition.

mockData.title: Einstein’s Mass–Energy Equivalence
mockData.subtitle: A revolutionary physics equation explaining the relationship between mass and energy.
mockData.description: Albert Einstein’s equation demonstrates that mass can be converted into energy and vice versa. Because the speed of light squared is an enormous value, even a small amount of mass can release an extraordinary amount of energy.
notes: The equation is a foundation of modern nuclear physics.
Energy and mass are interchangeable forms of the same entity.
The speed of light is approximately 3 × 10⁸ meters per second.

mockData.title: Python Function Example
mockData.subtitle: A simple Python function demonstrating how reusable code blocks work.
mockData.code:
def calculate_square(number):
    result = number * number
    return result

value = calculate_square(5)
print("Square:", value)
mockData.description: This Python example defines a reusable function named calculate_square() that accepts a number as input, multiplies it by itself, and returns the squared value. The function is then called with the value 5, and the result is displayed in the console.
points: Functions help organize and reuse code efficiently.
Parameters allow values to be passed into functions dynamically.
The return statement sends the result back to the caller.
Readable code structure improves maintainability.
